scenes.title: Convoy Commander & Assistant Convoy Commander
scenes.text: Welcome to Convoy Commander and Assistant Convoy Commander training for the 733rd Transportation Company. You will learn the CC and ACC requirements, and how to plan, brief and lead a convoy. Our example is a past exercise, the March BA FTX 2025 move to JBMDL.
onscreen: Past training exercise, shown for instruction only

scenes.title: Convoy Organization
scenes.text: A convoy breaks into serials and march units, each with a head, main body and trail. Our small example has two elements, called serials. The CC commands the convoy, and each serial commander runs a serial. Most SOPs put the ACC, the second in command, toward the rear. The CC and ACC never share a vehicle, so one incident cannot take out both leaders.
onscreen: ACC: usually toward the rear (per SOP)
CC and ACC: never the same vehicle

scenes.title: CC and ACC Duties
scenes.text: The CC plans, briefs, controls and reports to higher. The ACC takes command if the CC cannot continue, so train the ACC to the same standard. Per your SOP, the ACC may also stage vehicles, prevent straggling, and run recovery. At the 541st Transportation Company's evaluation, the CC and ACC briefed as a team.
onscreen: ACC takes over if the CC can't continue
Train the ACC to the CC standard
541st TC: CC + ACC brief as a team

scenes.title: Requirements for CC and ACC
scenes.ref: Unit SOP; AR 600-55; USARC Pam 56-1; STP 21-24
scenes.text: Your commander designates the CC and ACC, and your SOP sets rank and certification. The CC may be an officer or an NCO, depending on convoy size. Both must know AR 600-55, because the CC ensures every driver is licensed on their vehicle, and every truck has a vehicle commander or senior occupant. The ACC meets the same standard, ready to take command at any moment. Both must know the route and comms plan cold, build a strip map, complete a risk assessment, and lead the breakdown and casualty drills. At the 454th Transportation Company, new CCs shadowed an experienced CC, then needed 80 out of 100 to certify.
onscreen: CC: officer or NCO, by convoy size
Licensed drivers (AR 600-55); a VC or senior occupant per truck
ACC: same standard as the CC
Can do: route, comms, strip map, DD 2977, drills

scenes.title: Preparation: Troop Leading Procedures
scenes.text: Start troop leading procedures the moment you get the mission, and issue a warning order. A Battle Assembly move is usually known weeks out, so use the time between drills for recon, clearance and coordination. Recon the route, at least by map, then build the strip map, risk assessment, manifest and comms plan. Brief, take a back-brief, rehearse, and supervise with PCCs and PCIs. Keep one-third of the time, and give two-thirds to your Soldiers.

scenes.title: The Convoy Brief: March BA FTX 2025
scenes.ref: March BA FTX 2025: past exercise, example only
scenes.text: Here is the twelve-item agenda from the March BA FTX 2025 convoy brief. Many items match parts of a five-paragraph order, but it is a unit checklist, not an OPORD.

scenes.title: Items 1-2: Introduction
scenes.ref: March BA FTX 2025: past exercise, example only
scenes.text: In item one, the CC introduces themselves, the ACC and the serial commanders, and says which serial each leader rides with. Then the CC states the mission: move personnel and equipment from Reading to JBMDL and back. Item two: every Soldier brings paper and a writing utensil to write down times, checkpoints and callsigns.
onscreen: Say which serial each leader rides with
Mission: Reading to JBMDL and back
2. Bring paper and a writing utensil

scenes.title: Item 3: PCCs and PCIs
scenes.text: Item three is PCCs and PCIs. Every Soldier shows ID tags, a civilian license, a military license, CAC, ACH, gloves and a water source. Beyond the brief's list, check each vehicle's dispatch packet and accident forms. PMCS every truck with the dash ten TM, and fix or report faults before SP. Leaders also check the warning kit, fire extinguisher, basic issue items and tow bars.
onscreen: ID tags, CAC, ACH, gloves, water source
Also check: dispatch packet, accident forms
Warning kit, extinguisher, BII, tow bars

scenes.title: Item 4: Risk Assessment
scenes.text: Item four is the risk assessment, on DD Form 2977, the Deliberate Risk Assessment Worksheet. List hazards like traffic, construction, fatigue and weather, then assign controls like licensed drivers, a full brief, and fixed speeds and intervals. Overall risk is never lower than the highest residual risk of any hazard. This brief assessed the risk as Low, which still needs sign-off from the approval authority. If risk rises on the move, halt somewhere safe and get the approval authority's decision.
onscreen: March BA FTX: risk assessed LOW
Risk goes up? Safe halt, re-approval

scenes.title: Item 5: Convoy Manifest
scenes.ref: March BA FTX 2025: past exercise, example only
scenes.text: Item five is the manifest: 7 vehicles and 13 personnel in two serials. Vehicles include PLS and LMTV trucks. Every weapon and sensitive item, here an M4A1, is listed with an assigned custodian who keeps positive control the whole trip. The order of march comes from the manifest, so every driver knows their position and callsign.
onscreen: Order of march from the manifest

scenes.title: Item 6: Convoy Clearance
scenes.text: Item six is convoy clearance. On public highways, a convoy is six or more vehicles under one commander, or ten or more per hour on the same route. Clearance is requested on DD Form 1265, through channels to the Defense Movement Coordinator of the starting state. The March BA brief listed clearance as not necessary. The CC must know why, so confirm the basis with your movement NCO or S3 and keep it on file. A loaded PLS may still need a DD Form 1266 permit for size or weight.
onscreen: Or 10+ vehicles per hour, same route
Request: DD Form 1265 to origin-state DMC
March BA brief: not necessary (confirm basis with S3)
Know why; keep the answer on file
Loaded PLS: may need DD Form 1266

scenes.title: Item 7: Communications
scenes.text: Item seven is communications, in a PACE plan. Primary is JBCP: keep messages short, use callsigns, and acknowledge. Secondary, the alternate, is the radio on the frequency from the SOI. Tertiary, the contingency, is a cell phone group chat, which is not secure, so keep sensitive details off it and never text while driving. Add an emergency method from your SOP, and check every method before SP. Callsigns are Stampede plus the vehicle or position number.
onscreen: Tertiary (contingency): cell group chat, not secure
A passenger texts, never the driver
Add an emergency method (not in this brief)

scenes.title: Item 8: Fuel Cards and Fuel Points
scenes.text: Item eight is fuel cards, one with the Serial 1 commander and one with the Serial 2 commander. Sign for them, keep every receipt, and turn them in. At every fuel stop and halt, the custodian keeps the weapon under positive control, and its vehicle is never left unattended. Outbound, the fuel point is the Love's at checkpoint 6. On the return trip, it is the King of Prussia, or KOP, Travel Plaza on I-76 West.
onscreen: Sign for cards, keep every receipt
Weapons/SI: never unattended at fuel or halts
Return fuel: KOP Travel Plaza, I-76 W

scenes.title: Item 9: Route and Strip Map
scenes.ref: March BA FTX 2025: past exercise, example only
scenes.text: Item nine is the route and strip map. Serial 1 crosses the SP at the 733rd TC in Reading at 0730, and Serial 2 at 0800. Checkpoints 1 through 4 are I-176 South, I-76 East, I-276 East and I-95 North. Checkpoints 5 through 8 are Exit 7 to Route 206 South, the Love's fuel point, the JBMDL post gate, and the left turn onto Range Road. Serial 1 reaches the RP at about 1000, and Serial 2 at about 1030. Every vehicle carries a strip map marked with the halts and nearest hospitals.
onscreen: CKPT 7-8: JBMDL gate, L on Range Rd

scenes.title: Item 9: X-Checks
scenes.ref: March BA FTX 2025 (past exercise); unit SOP
scenes.text: The brief also set three X-checks: the SP, the Delaware River, and the RP. At each one, every vehicle answers a roll call by callsign to its serial commander. The river is the state line, a landmark no one can miss. The CC confirms all 7 vehicles and 13 Soldiers across both serials, then reports to higher. Your SOP defines what an X-check includes.
onscreen: Roll call by callsign, per serial
Serial CDR to CC, CC to higher

scenes.title: Item 9: Speed, Interval and Terrain
scenes.ref: March BA FTX 2025 (past exercise); USARC Pam 56-1
scenes.text: On the highway, this brief set intervals of 50 to 75 meters. March speed is 5 miles per hour below the posted limit, or lower if a TM or command cap requires it. If the rear falls behind, the lead slows, and the rear closes up at catch-up speed, the posted limit, never above a TM or SOP cap. Intervals vary by unit SOP, road and speed. Confirm yours, and open it up as speed rises and on wet roads.
onscreen: Speed: 5 below posted, or TM/SOP cap
Catch-up: posted limit, capped by TM/SOP
Interval per SOP: varies by road, speed
Open it up for speed and wet roads

scenes.title: Item 9: Distance Between Serials
scenes.text: Serial 2 leaves the SP 30 minutes after Serial 1. If Serial 2 can see Serial 1, it is too close, so Serial 2 makes space. The gap keeps the serials from merging and lets each one clear the fuel point. The serial commanders manage that gap on comms.
onscreen: No merging into one long column
Each serial clears the fuel point

scenes.title: Item 10: Convoy Contingency Plan
scenes.ref: March BA FTX 2025 (past exercise); USARC Pam 56-1
scenes.text: Item ten is the convoy contingency plan, and the recovery assets are tow bars. If a vehicle breaks down, the driver turns on the 4-ways, pulls safely off the road, and reports to the CC and ACC, who report up. West of KOP, the vehicle is recovered back to the unit. East of KOP, it is recovered forward to JBMDL to continue the mission. The crew sets out warning triangles per SOP, then waits well away from traffic, behind the guardrail if possible. Tow with a vehicle the same size or larger, chains on, per the TM. Put CLS-trained Soldiers and aid bags in each serial. For an accident or injury, call 9-1-1, render aid, report up, and hold the scene for the police report.
onscreen: West of KOP: back to unit
East of KOP: recovered forward to JBMDL
Warning triangles out; crew clear of traffic
Tow: same size or larger, chains on (TM)
CLS + aid bags each serial; accident: 9-1-1, aid, report

scenes.title: Item 11: Safety
scenes.text: Item eleven is safety. The weather line is filled in on brief day, so check the forecast and brief it. The road hazard is construction, so expect lane shifts, narrow lanes and sudden stops. Seat belts and headlights stay on, flags and signs go up per SOP, and drivers are rested. Assistant drivers, where assigned, stay awake, and no one lets a tired driver drive.
onscreen: Weather: check forecast on brief day
Convoy flags and signs per SOP
No tired driver behind the wheel

scenes.title: Item 12: Back-Brief
scenes.text: Item twelve is the back-brief and check on learning. Instead of asking whether everyone understands, call on specific Soldiers. What is Serial 2's SP time, and what is our secondary comms? Your truck breaks down east of KOP, so what do you do? Then serial commanders back-brief how they will run their serials, and the convoy rehearses the breakdown drill and comms check.
onscreen: 4-ways, triangles, report. Recovered forward to JBMDL.
Serial commanders, back-brief your plan. Then we rehearse.

scenes.title: Executing the Convoy
scenes.text: On mission day, line up in order of march, confirm accountability, and run a final comms check. Cross the SP on time, and report at each X-check or other SOP reporting point. The ACC makes sure no one is left behind. At halts, get fully off the road and check vehicles and people. At the RP, report closure, account for everyone and every sensitive item, and lead an AAR.
onscreen: Report at each X-check / SOP reporting point
Halts: off the road, check vehicles

scenes.title: Case Study: Unauthorized Driver Swap
scenes.text: This example comes from an Army safety article on DVIDS called Training Tragedy. A company convoyed 13 vehicles to training. After the brief, the crew of the third load handling truck swapped drivers without telling the convoy commander. The new driver was unlicensed and inexperienced on that truck. When the truck ahead stopped, the new driver could not stop in time and hit it at about 50 to 55 miles per hour, and the driver was killed. Enforce licensing and interval, make vehicle commanders own their trucks, and allow no unapproved driver swaps.
onscreen: New driver: unlicensed on that truck
Rear-end crash at 50-55 mph, driver killed

scenes.title: Knowledge Check
scenes.text: Knowledge check. 8 questions. Answer each one before the answer appears, and pause the video if you need more time.

scenes.title: Question 1 of 8
scenes.ref: March BA FTX 2025: past exercise, example only
scenes.text: On the way to JBMDL, a truck breaks down east of KOP, so where does it go: A, back to the unit, B, on to JBMDL, or C, left in place until after the FTX? Answer: B, it is recovered forward to JBMDL.
onscreen: C. Left in place until after the FTX
scenes.question: On the way to JBMDL, a truck breaks down east of KOP. Where does it go?
choices: Left in place until after the FTX

scenes.title: Question 2 of 8
scenes.text: In most unit SOPs, where does the ACC ride: A, in the CC's vehicle, B, in the lead vehicle, or C, toward the rear? Answer: C, toward the rear, never with the CC.
onscreen: In most SOPs, where does the ACC ride?
scenes.question: In most unit SOPs, where does the ACC ride?

scenes.title: Question 3 of 8
scenes.ref: March BA FTX 2025: past exercise, example only
scenes.text: Who carries the fuel cards in this brief: A, the CC, B, each serial commander, or C, every driver? Answer: B, each serial commander.
scenes.question: In this brief, who carries the fuel cards?

scenes.title: Question 4 of 8
scenes.text: Which form is the Deliberate Risk Assessment Worksheet: A, DD Form 1265, B, DD Form 2977, or C, DA Form 5988-E? Answer: B, DD Form 2977.
scenes.question: Which form is the Deliberate Risk Assessment Worksheet?

scenes.title: Question 5 of 8
scenes.ref: March BA FTX 2025 (past exercise); USARC Pam 56-1
scenes.text: In this brief, what is catch-up speed: A, 5 over the limit, B, the posted limit, or C, whatever it takes? Answer: B, the posted limit, capped by any TM or command limit.
scenes.question: In this brief, what is catch-up speed?

scenes.title: Question 6 of 8
scenes.text: Which form requests convoy clearance: A, DD Form 1265, B, DD Form 1266, or C, DD Form 2977? Answer: A, DD Form 1265.
scenes.question: Which form requests convoy clearance?

scenes.title: Question 7 of 8
scenes.ref: March BA FTX 2025: past exercise, example only
scenes.text: Serial 2 can see Serial 1, so what does Serial 2 do: A, close up and join, B, pass, or C, make space? Answer: C, make space and coordinate on comms.
onscreen: Serial 2 can see Serial 1. Now what?
A. Close up and join Serial 1
scenes.question: Serial 2 can see Serial 1. What does Serial 2 do?

scenes.title: Question 8 of 8
scenes.text: Before SP, whose licensing must the CC confirm: A, only the lead driver, B, every driver, on their vehicle, or C, only the CC and ACC? Answer: B, every driver, on their vehicle.
onscreen: Whose licensing does the CC confirm?
B. Every driver, on their vehicle
C. Only the CC and ACC
scenes.question: Before SP, whose licensing must the CC confirm?

scenes.title: Recap
scenes.text: To recap, the CC leads the convoy, and the ACC is ready to take command. Your commander designates both, and your SOP sets the requirements. Brief all twelve items, enforce the standards, and close every mission with an AAR.
onscreen: Finish every mission with an AAR

scenes.title: References
scenes.text: Check each edition of these references, the DTR Part III appendix and your 733rd TC SOP before you teach. Plan it, brief it, lead it, and bring every Soldier home.
